rv.q: Her sharp observations and crackling dialogue were evident in her earlier playwriting, too and, in director Rhiann Jeffery's taut new production, feel fresh and current.

She was among the many readers who saw themselves in the characters’ struggles; the book became a national bestseller and introduced a boom of memoirs about young women and mental illness. Zollo later brought the idea of adaptation to her parents, both producers; her mother, Barbara Broccoli, controlled the James Bond franchise for decades.
In its strongest moments, the adaptation captures the riptide sensation of being pulled far from safe shores.
Fans of Mann and Marjok, as well as theatergoers truly interested in viewing fresh, vital, new works of music drama should try to get a ticket to this compelling production.
However, it falls short of developing the characters into people the audience can really feel for.
There's plenty of beautiful, delicate, heartfelt work in the mix. But whatever the blend of complicating pathologies, this girl still feels fettered.
